what_is.question: What is Decentraland?
what_is.answer: Launched in 2020, Decentraland is a virtual social world, the first decentralized metaverse, and the only one that is open source. Within the Decentraland platform, which can run on a browser or desktop app, users can create, experience, and monetize content and applications as well as socialize and attend a wide range of daily, community-driven events. Decentraland is unique in that it is owned, created, and governed by the people who use it every day. Through Decentraland's decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) users can submit and vote on proposals and even apply for grants for the community to vote on.

what_create.question: What can I create in Decentraland?
what_create.answer:
It would be easier to ask what you can't create in Decentraland! As a virtual world created by its users, in Decentraland you can create just about everything.
Decentraland Creators make all the components that go into crafting a digital identity, such as Wearables (this can include whole skins, body parts, articles of clothing, hair styles, accessories, etc.) as well as Emotes, animations for your avatar which can include props and sounds in addition to movement.
The landscape and activities of Decentraland are also all shaped by creators. Walking through Decentraland's Genesis City, you can explore a variety of content from different creators, built side-by-side: art galleries, theaters, gardens, night clubs, racetracks, casinos, entire game experiences, and more can be explored and created by everyone! To start building, download Decentraland's Creator Hub.

become_creator.question: How do I become a Decentraland creator?
become_creator.answer:
Anyone can be a Decentraland creator, all it takes is a little knowhow and endless creative ideas! Depending on what you want to create, the knowledge you need to know differs. If you just want to create cool virtual scenes for yourself or to host events, and learning programming and 3D modeling isn't in your plans, then you can get started creating scenes right away by downloading Decentraland's Creator Hub.

For those familiar with or willing to learn 3D modeling and/or programming, all the technical specs and procedures you need to know to create in Decentraland can be found on the Creator Docs page, and there are many tutorials available online for creating Wearables, Emotes, and experiences.
Wearables & Emotes
The process of creating Wearables & Emotes involves asset creation in a 3D modeling program like Blender, submission to the Curation Committee who ensure that your creation is technically sound and complies with Decentraland's content policy (this includes the publication fee of 25 USD per item, which goes to the DAO to fund community grants; for a limited time, the Decentraland Foundation covers 20 USD, so you pay only 5 USD per item). Finally, once your creation is approved, it is officially published in the Marketplace! You'll receive 97.5% of all primary sales and earn 2.5% royalties on any secondary sales.
Experiences
If you're interested in designing experiences, download Decentraland's Creator Hub and you can start creating immersive scenes and games which you can then publish to Worlds or LAND in Decentraland's open-world Genesis City. You retain all control over your content, can edit or remove it whenever you wish, and keep all proceeds of any funds you may generate through your experiences.

monetize.question: Is it possible to monetize my creations?
monetize.answer:
Yes, of course! Decentraland creators are able to monetize their skills in many ways.

Wearable and Emote creators publish their creations in the Marketplace with a publication fee of 25 USD per item, which goes to the DAO to fund community grants (for a limited time, the Decentraland Foundation covers 20 USD, so creators pay only 5 USD per item), and as a result earn 97.5% of the profits on all primary sales and 2.5% royalties on any secondary sales.
Some scene creators monetize their experiences, the revenue of which they are able to keep fully for themselves.

need_land.question: Do I need to own LAND to create experiences in Decentraland?
need_land.answer:
No, owning LAND is not necessary to create scenes or interactive experiences in Decentraland. Anyone is free to create content using Decentraland's SDK 7 or no-code Editor. Then, if you want to publish your creations so that you and others can explore and enjoy them, there are multiple options available to you, in addition to owning LAND.
Worlds
Worlds are your personal 3D space in the metaverse. They exist separately from the open-world map of Decentraland's Genesis City and are perfect for those looking to experiment with 3D creation or host their own virtual space.

Getting your own World is easy: when you claim a Decentraland NAME (100 MANA) you not only get a unique username that can be used across Web3, but also 100 Voting Power (used in Decentraland governance), and of course your own World to use as you wish.

Rent LAND
If you're interested in publishing your content in Decentraland's open-world Genesis City but don't want to commit to a LAND purchase, you don't have to! It's easy to rent LAND for the short or long term in the Marketplace where you can pay by card, bank transfer, or cryptocurrency. Browse rentals and see what's available!

Community Connections, Community Grants, and Open Calls for Creators
If someone is passionate about sharing their creations with the community, in Decentraland there will always be a way to make it happen. The creator community is very welcoming and open to lending a hand. If you're just getting started, you can meet many creators in the Community Building Discord.
If you want to build an experience that benefits the community, but need the resources to make it happen, you can always try applying for a Community Grant in the DAO. You may also apply to one of the Open Calls that happen periodically through the year to build experiences and scenes for various Decentraland events such as the annual music, art, and fashion festivals. Stay tuned to Decentraland socials or subscribe to the weekly newsletter to stay updated!

need_crypto.question: Do I need cryptocurrency or a digital wallet to use Decentraland?
need_crypto.answer:
You do not need to own cryptocurrency to enjoy Decentraland as it is free to use. If you decide to purchase a community-made creation from the Marketplace, there are multiple payment options available, such as credit/debit card and bank transfer in addition to various cryptocurrencies.

As for owning a digital wallet, if you don't already have one, you don't need to get one yourself if you don't want to. When you sign in to Decentraland for the first time, creating your account, a digital wallet will be created for you behind the scenes. It's as simple as that!

This digital wallet is part of your Decentraland account and is used to store any digital assets you acquire, such as free Wearables you might claim in-world or a fun Emote you purchase in the Marketplace.

error.root: The approval could not be put on chain. Nothing was uploaded; try again.
error.deploy: Some items could not be uploaded or approved. Try again to retry the ones that failed.

linked_approval_flow.changed: The pending items changed since you opened them: items were added or edited. Review them again before approving.

stage.build: its content changed or could not be prepared
stage.deploy: the upload to the content servers failed
stage.curation: it was uploaded, but marking it approved failed
stage.changed: the creator edited it during the approval, so it was sent back to them to submit again

linked_approval_flow.unsubmitted: The creator saved changes to items after submitting them, and hasn't submitted those changes for review. They need to submit them again before these items can be approved.

has_video.title: These items can't be approved yet
has_video.description: {items} include a preview video, which the content servers don't accept for linked items. Nothing was put on chain. The creator needs to upload them again without the video.

notice.automated_reviewing: We're running an automated review of your collection. This usually takes a few minutes.
notice.awaiting_curator: Automated review passed. Your collection is now waiting for a curator's review.
notice.human_review: A curator will review your collection.
notice.needs_curator: The automated review couldn't run on your collection. It's now waiting for a curator's review.
notice.appealed: You asked for a human review. A curator will look at your collection.
notice.rejected_by_validator: The automated review found issues in your items. Fix them and review again, or ask a curator to review your collection.
notice.rejected_by_curator: A curator requested fixes on your collection. Update your items, then request review again.
notice.curator_comments: {count, plural, one {A curator left you a comment} other {A curator left you # comments}}

reviewing.title: Reviewing collection
reviewing.description: An automated review is checking your collection. In about 5 minutes you'll know whether it's ready for a curator or needs fixes.

review_flow.attempts_tooltip: You can run up to {max} automated reviews per day. Once you reach the limit, you can request a curator review or wait until the next day (00:00 UTC) to try again.

issues.title: Some items need your attention
issues.intro: We found a few issues that need to be resolved before your collection can move on to a curator. Fix them and review again, or request a curator review if you think they were flagged by mistake.

request.title: Request curator review?
request.description: If you believe the detected issues are incorrect, you can request a review from a Decentraland curator. Curator reviews take more time. We'll notify you once the review is complete.
request.note_placeholder: Say why you think the issues don't apply

sent.title: Collection sent for review!
sent.description: Your collection has been sent to a Decentraland curator for review. Curator reviews take more time. We'll notify you once the review is complete, whether your collection is approved or needs changes.

limit.title: Daily automated review limit reached
limit.description: You've reached the limit of {max} automated reviews per day. You can request a manual review from a Decentraland curator, which may take a little longer, or try again in {time}, when your reviews reset.
limit.description_wait: You've reached the limit of {max} automated reviews per day. Try again in {time}, when your reviews reset.

additional.title: Your collection needs an additional review
additional.description: Some content in your collection requires a closer look. We've sent it to a Decentraland curator for review. Curator reviews take more time. We'll notify you once it's approved or if any changes are needed.

review_flow.no_changes: Nothing has changed since the last automated review. Update your items to review again.
review_flow.running: A review is already running. Try again when it finishes.
review_flow.nothing_to_validate: There's nothing new for the automated review. Edit an item and publish your changes, or request a curator review.
review_flow.busy: The collection is being updated, try again in a moment.
review_flow.appeal_open: A curator review was already requested for this collection.
review_flow.appeal_error: We couldn't send your request. Please try again.
review_flow.validation_started: Automated review started. We'll update this page when it finishes.
review_flow.validation_error: We couldn't start the automated review. Please try again.

review_stage_hint.rejected_by_validator: Fixes requested by the automated review.

findings.item_unsupported: Not covered by the automated review
findings.item_error: The automated review couldn't check it: {error}

reject_curation_modal.title: Request fixes
reject_curation_modal.heading: Select the reasons
reject_curation_modal.message_placeholder: Tell the creator what to fix. They'll see this, so be specific.
reject_curation_modal.error: We couldn't send the request. Please try again.

automated_verdict.title: Automated review
automated_verdict.banner_issues: Issues in {failed} of {total, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}
automated_verdict.button_passed: Automated review passed. Click to see the details.
automated_verdict.status_unsupported: Some items can't be reviewed automatically
automated_verdict.reason_requested: The creator requested a curator review
automated_verdict.button_unsupported: Some items can't be reviewed automatically. Click to see the details.
automated_verdict.button_rejected: Automated review found issues. Click to see the details.

activity_modal.title: Activity
activity_modal.unavailable: This collection has no activity timeline yet.
activity_modal.error: We couldn't load the activity of this collection.

event.review.human_required: Sent to the curation committee (third-party collection)
event.review.human_required_unsupported: Some items can't go through the automated review, a curator will review them
event.review.automated_rejected: Automated review found issues in {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}
event.review.automated_error_curator: Automated review failed and will be retried
event.changes.submitted: submitted changes to {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}

review.automated_error_final: The automated review couldn't run on this collection, a curator will review it

comment.placeholder_creator: Ask a question, say what you changed or answer a curator's comment
comment.placeholder_curator: Ask a question or tell the creator what to look at
comment.error: We couldn't send your message. Please try again.

wallet_error.wrong_account: Your wallet switched to another account or network. Switch it back to the account you signed in with and try again.

preview_controls.move: Move the camera up or down
